seoTitle: URL Encode / Decode - Parse Web Addresses
metaDescription: Free online URL Encoder and Decoder. Safely encode special characters for URL parameters, or decode messy web addresses into readable text.
intro: Dealing with broken links or messy URL parameters? Our free URL Encode/Decode tool translates spaces and special characters into safe web formats instantly.
whatIs: The URL Encode/Decode tool is a web development utility. It converts characters that are not allowed in web addresses (like spaces, ampersands, or question marks) into safe 'percent-encoded' formats, and vice versa.
howToUse: Select whether you want to 'Encode' or 'Decode'.
Paste your text or messy URL into the input field.
The tool instantly parses the string and provides the converted URL.
howItWorks: URL Encoding (Percent-encoding) replaces unsafe ASCII characters with a '%' followed by their two-digit hexadecimal equivalent. The tool uses standard browser APIs (`encodeURIComponent` and `decodeURIComponent`) to execute this perfectly.
workedExample: If you encode the string 'Hello World!', the space is not allowed in a URL. The tool replaces the space with '%20' and the exclamation point with '%21', resulting in 'Hello%20World%21'.
resultInterpretation: The encoded result can be safely appended to a web URL or API request without breaking the link. The decoded result turns a messy link back into readable, human text.
useCases: Web Analytics: Building UTM tracking links that contain spaces or special characters in the campaign name.
API Development: Safely passing complex JSON data or search queries as a URL parameter.
Debugging: Decoding a long, confusing URL copied from a web browser to read exactly what parameters are being passed.
tipsAndLimitations: Be careful not to encode an entire, already-valid URL (like 'https://google.com'). It will encode the colons and slashes, breaking the link. Only encode the specific parameters or paths.
In modern URL encoding, spaces are converted to '%20', though in older form submissions they were sometimes converted to '+'.

faq.question: What is Percent Encoding?
faq.answer: Percent encoding is the official mechanism for encoding information in a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI). It guarantees that URLs only contain universally accepted, safe ASCII characters.

faq.question: Why did my link break?
faq.answer: URLs cannot contain spaces or certain special characters (like ?, &, =, #) because those characters have specific programmatic meanings in a web browser. Encoding prevents these errors.

cta: Encode or decode your URLs instantly!
disclaimer: Tool uses strict URI component encoding. Be sure to only encode the query parameters, not the base protocol (http://) of the link.
